parsed.explanation: A trans visitor who is outed faces active, recently intensified criminal enforcement, not merely a dormant statute. Article 319 now carries 5–10 years, the 2026 amendment bans promotion/support of transsexuality, arrests are documented through 2026 including at a border post, and trans people are described as often prosecuted and violently targeted. Documented custody torture, long sentences, mob exhumation/burning and goor-gigen grave desecration show severe consequences and thin recourse, though no death penalty or current routine-torture pattern is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Border-post detention documented in Feb 2026 during attempted departure; no sourced evidence on passport-marker screening itself.
entry_documents.interaction: Departure/border encounter can convert disclosure into investigation under Article 319.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Repeated arrests, including on second-hand reports and after videos; 2008-09 custody torture documented; Oct sentences of 3-4 years.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some releases/bail and 2009 overturned convictions show occasional remedy, but no effective pattern documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presentation/association can lead to prolonged custody, ill-treatment risk, then prosecution.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facilities and custody placement by gender identity not documented; no legal gender recognition is resident-facing and not counted as visitor exposure.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented how detention or hospital placement would treat a foreign trans visitor.

care_services.exposure: No current evidence on visitor HRT, clinic access or medication seizure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 319 increased to 5-10 years; 2026 ban on promotion/financing/support of transsexuality and LGBT organisations/media; enforcement documented and ongoing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Limited prohibitions on stigmatising depiction only; no broad anti-discrimination protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State hostility legitimises societal violence and makes visibility/advocacy itself risky.

minors_guardians.exposure: Maximum penalty always applies where act involves person under 21; travelling with a minor increases exposure if any allegation arises.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor companion or young adult could trigger the maximum-penalty provision and heightened scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented physical violence, 2023 exhumation and street burning of outed gay man before crowd, and 2009 goor-gigen disinterments; trans people face intolerance and violence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Four suspected masterminds apprehended in 2023; otherwise no documented effective protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social hostility plus criminalisation discourages reporting and leaves mob violence largely unchecked.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 2026 promotion-ban prosecutions, August 99-arrest date, border marker practice and current trans-specific prevalence are not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts occasionally overturn or release, but no timely, reliable remedy documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns do not offset documented enforcement; incident list is stated to be a floor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in active arrests, long imprisonment and custody abuse, but this case lacks a capital provision and lacks documented current routine beatings, so it sits slightly above 0.15.
More severe than 0.25: sentences are years not short jail, the statute was recently doubled, transsexuality is explicitly targeted, and lethal mob desecration is documented.
Well below 0.35, where exclusion without imprisonment is the outcome; here prosecution, multi-year prison and violent societal targeting are documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national criminal law, 2026 anti-transsexuality promotion ban, police enforcement surges and societal hostility interact so disclosure at a hotel, video, border or street encounter can trigger arrest and prison, while fear and stigma suppress remedy. Occasional releases and an arrest of attackers in one mob case are weaker than the documented pattern. No operative visitor protection offsets this. Minors/young companions raise penalty exposure. Overall severe risk short of the execution tier.
